corpus.note: Line numbers are valid only for this commit. Clone with --depth 1 and point LABPILOT_GEO_SRC at the checkout before scoring. The source is NOT committed: it is third-party code, and the provenance rule keeps it out of the repository.

why: THE THIRD FIXTURE, and it exists to break two monocultures at once.

Language: both older corpora are Python, so every retrieval number this project has recorded describes ONE language. Go has no AST splitter here, so this is also the first corpus measured through split_recursive - and its chunk headers carry NO function label, only file and lines.

Domain: quora is machine learning and requests is an HTTP client. This is computational geometry on the sphere - tolerances, epsilons, cell hierarchies, exact predicates. It is the closest fixture in the project to LabPilot's own pitch of a paper against a solver.
Size: 729 chunks, so a 50-document window is 7% of the corpus, against 15% on requests and 61% on the 30-document quora runs. The FIRST fixture with a production-like window ratio.

ORDER: the categories are INTERLEAVED, deliberately. requests/queries.json is grouped by `asks`, so its first k queries are a category study wearing a corpus study's clothes - which is exactly how the 2026-09-11 Voyage run produced a biased 8-query result. Here any prefix is a stratified sample.

fields.file: the file holding the answer, relative to the repository root
fields.expects: the lines in that file that really answer the question
fields.asks: what kind of thing the question wants: constant, behaviour, error, api, structure
fields.wording: named = the question uses a word that also appears in the code. paraphrase = the question deliberately avoids the words the code uses. NEITHER may contain the identifier being searched for, or the run measures string matching instead of retrieval.
